functions: command metric aggregation over the flattened command list

contracts.shape: { id, color, name, stitch_type, priority, points: Array<[x, y]>, layerType, ... }
contracts.notes: objects carry geometry as point arrays; no per-stitch command exists yet at this layer
tie-in, underlay and tie-off are injected here; the lab model deliberately produces none of them

contracts.shape: { type, x, y, color, regionId, stitchType?, source?, layerType? }
contracts.units: mm, ABSOLUTE needle position per command (not deltas)
contracts.xyMeaning: absolute needle position after applying the export offset
contracts.objectBoundaryRepresentation: no explicit begin/end object command; object boundaries are implied by regionId changes plus trim / colorChange commands emitted between objects

contracts.units: 0.1 mm units; DST delta range ±121 (±12.1 mm), DSB signed byte range ±127 (±12.7 mm)
contracts.notes: relative representation; long moves are split at the encoder level

contractDifferences: productive commands are per-POINT (absolute needle position), the lab model is per-SEGMENT (fromMm → toMm with delta and length)
productive commands use `type`, `x`, `y`; the lab model uses `op`, `fromMm`, `toMm`
productive commands require object/colour context (color, regionId); the lab model is intentionally context-free and local to one column
productive flow injects tie-in / underlay / tie-off and control ops (jump, trim, colorChange, end) that the lab model forbids
encoders work in 0.1 mm relative units; the lab model keeps full-precision absolute mm and never quantizes
productive flow subdivides long stitches; the lab model only reports splitRequired
risks: an adapter must add color, regionId and object sequencing, none of which the lab model can invent
an adapter must decide how the first point becomes an entry move (jump vs stitch) — a sequencing decision that belongs to the caller, not to a single column
quantization to 0.1 mm units at encoder level will change measured lengths; the lab model's exactness must not be read as machine exactness
underlay and pull compensation are absent by design, so a lab model is not a производственный stitch plan
unverifiableFields: presence of an explicit object-begin command: none found in the inspected code (boundaries are implied), so it cannot be mapped
canonical TypeScript/JSON schema for productive commands: no schema file found; the contract is implicit in flattenToCommands and its consumers

futureCompatibility.rationale: every lab command maps 1:1 to a productive { type: 'stitch', x, y } command by emitting toMm as the absolute position (with startAnchorMm emitted first by the caller), but color, regionId, entry/exit moves, tie stitches and underlay must be supplied by an adapter that P1.F1 does not implement
